panels.headline: Shift from solitary reasoning to collaborative endeavors in multi-agent systems
content: Multi-agent systems (MAS) extend LLMs from independent reasoning to system-level intelligence.
Recent advances in MAS have shifted the paradigm to collaborative efforts among multiple models.
LLM-based MAS has been adopted in various applications, including math and science reasoning, open-domain QA, and robotics.
Text-based mediation is commonly used for reasoning and communication, but latent space collaboration is underexplored.

panels.headline: Achieve pure latent collaboration without text-based mediation
content: Can MAS achieve pure latent collaboration without relying on text-based mediation?
How can latent collaboration enhance system-level reasoning quality and efficiency in MAS?

panels.headline: LatentMAS: Training-free framework for pure latent collaboration
content: LatentMAS is an end-to-end training-free framework enabling pure latent collaboration among LLM agents.
Each agent generates auto-regressive latent thoughts through last-layer hidden embeddings.
A shared latent working memory, stored in layer-wise KV caches, ensures lossless information exchange.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of LatentMAS. Each LLM agent generates latent thoughts through last-layer hidden states, then transfers information layer-wise via shared latent working memory.

panels.headline: Evaluated on 9 benchmarks with 3 LLM model scales
content: Empirical evaluations were conducted on nine benchmarks spanning math, science reasoning, commonsense understanding, and code generation.
Experiments were performed under both sequential and hierarchical MAS settings with three backbone scales (4B, 8B, and 14B).
panels.figure_caption: Evaluation of LatentMAS across accuracy performance, inference speed, and token usage over 9 benchmarks and 3 LLM model scales under the Hierarchical MAS setting.

panels.headline: Accuracy 87.8%, 4×-4.3× faster, 70.8%-83.7% token reduction
content: LatentMAS consistently outperformed strong single-model and text-based MAS baselines, achieving up to 14.6% higher accuracy.
Inference was 4 × -4.3 × faster and token usage was reduced by 70.8%-83.7%.
Latent thought expressiveness, working-memory transfer, and input-output alignment were confirmed to be semantically meaningful, lossless, and stable.
panels.figure_caption: Main results of LatentMAS on 6 general tasks under the Sequential MAS setting. We report accuracy, token usage, and end-to-end speed, and highlight the performance gains.

panels.headline: Latent collaboration enhances reasoning quality and efficiency
content: Latent collaboration in multi-agent systems enhances system-level reasoning quality while offering substantial efficiency gains without additional training.
LatentMAS is a promising approach for future research in collaborative AI systems.
The framework is currently limited to LLMs and may not be directly applicable to other types of models.
